entries.title: Seoul Welcome Week: Free Heritage Passes Are Now at Airport Counters, While Supplies Last
entries.paragraph_1: Seoul began distributing free Heritage Edition Discover Seoul Passes at airport tourist information counters today — September 19, 2026 — the first day of a 23-day welcome campaign timed to coincide with four overlapping East Asian holiday clusters. The passes, which give foreign arrivals free entry to 12 Joseon-era heritage sites including Seoul's four major royal palaces and Jongmyo Shrine, are available on a first-come, first-served basis at Incheon and Gimpo airports. There is no guarantee of supply; the city describes the distribution as reaching "a limited number of foreign visitors," and the supply will likely face its heaviest pressure during Japan's Silver Week — which also started today — and again during China's National Day holiday from October 1 to 7.
entries.paragraph_2: The 2026 Seoul Welcome Week: Autumn Edition runs through October 11 and is co-hosted by the Seoul Metropolitan Government, the Seoul Tourism Organization, and the Seoul Tourism Association . The program is Seoul's most geographically expansive Welcome Week to date, extending from airport arrival halls to tourist information centers citywide — a deliberate shift, according to the city, from earlier campaigns that concentrated activity in Myeongdong.

entries.title: South Korea's Hormuz dilemma reaches Washington as Cho meets Rubio | IBTimes JP
entries.paragraph_1: South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun met U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Washington on Friday for the first formal bilateral talks between the two ministers since February. The meeting brought into sharp focus a question Seoul has been unable to answer for six months: whether South Korea will send military assets to the Strait of Hormuz.
entries.paragraph_2: The meeting had been seven months in the making. In March, President Donald Trump asked South Korea, Japan, China and several European countries to dispatch warships to the strait, presenting the request as a test of allied solidarity as the U.S.-Israeli campaign against Iran entered its third week. Seoul initially responded with studied ambiguity. Cho told the National Assembly that he could not confirm whether a formal request had even been made, saying only that any decision would comply with the Constitution and domestic law — a formulation that bought time without closing off any options.

entries.paragraph_1: Let it be clear. There will be no dispatch of troops that will lead to involvement in a conflict. There will be no engagement or involvement in war, Lee said in a press conference. The South Korean president said it was also clear that the country needs to conduct the minimum level of activities to safeguard nationals or the transportation route for crude oil in the area, as other countries do, Yonhap reported. South Korea's Cheonghae military unit has expanded the scope of its mission to carry out relevant activities in the area, but it is true that we are reviewing and thinking about ways to strengthen (measures) on this, Lee said. Earlier in August, US President Donald Trump said in a Truth Social post that he had recently asked Lee whether South Korea would join the US in the Denuclearization of the Islamic Republic of Iran, but received a negative response. While somewhat unrelated (?), I recently asked the President of South Korea if they would like to join us in the Denuclearization of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and they said, No thanks! Thank you for your attention to this matter, Trump said. Trump also said that he had ordered a substantial reduction in the annual joint military exercises with South Korea, citing their cost, his very good relationship with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and concerns that the drills send an inappropriate and hostile signal to Pyongyang. Based on my very good relationship with Kim Jong Un, of North Korea, I was not happy with the fact that the United States had, long ago, agreed to participate in Joint Military Exercises with South Korea, Trump said. Meanwhile, on domestic issues, Lee reaffirmed that he had no intention of seeking reelection through constitutional revision, also noting that his reelection is impossible under the Constitution, according to Yonhap. I once again make it clear that I have no intention to seek reelection, he told a televised press conference. The South Korean president's remarks follow repeated calls from the opposition bloc for him to declare his intentions, accusing him of seeking reelection, despite a constitutional clause that stipulates any changes to the presidential system shall not apply to the president in office at the time of a revision. Friday's event marked the seventh press conference by the president since he took office in June 2025, but a rare one, given that most of his previous press conferences were held on and around special occasions, such as the first anniversary of his administration. The event, announced three days earlier, comes after Lee saw his approval ratings decline to the lowest levels in the mid-30 per cent range in recent weeks, especially among young voters, Yonhap reported. entries.title: “No troop dispatch”: South Korea's President Lee stresses need to protect national interests in Hormuz
entries.paragraph_1: ANI | Updated: Sep 18, 2026 09:53 IST
entries.paragraph_2: Seoul [South Korea], September 18 (ANI): South Korean President Lee Jae Myung on Friday ruled out any troop dispatch that could lead to the country's involvement in an overseas conflict. He stressed the need to protect South Korean citizens and national interests in the Strait of Hormuz, according to Yonhap News Agency. “Let it be clear. There will be no dispatch of troops that will lead to involvement in a conflict. There will be no engagement or involvement in war,” Lee said in a press conference. The South Korean president said it was also clear that the country needs to conduct “the minimum level of activities” to safeguard nationals or the transportation route for crude oil in the area, as other countries do, Yonhap reported. South Korea's Cheonghae military unit has expanded the scope of its mission to carry out relevant activities in the area, but “it is true that we are reviewing and thinking about ways to strengthen (measures) on this,” Lee said. Earlier in August, US President Donald Trump said in a Truth Social post that he had recently asked Lee whether South Korea would join the US in the “Denuclearization of the Islamic Republic of Iran”, but received a negative response. “While somewhat unrelated (?), I recently asked the President of South Korea if they would like to join us in the Denuclearization of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and they said, ‘No thanks!’ Thank you for your attention to this matter,” Trump said.

entries.title: North Korea Won’t Give Up Nuclear Weapons, Kim’s Sister Says
entries.paragraph_1: The powerful sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, Kim Yo Jong, has declared that the country’s status as a nuclear-armed state is “absolute,” dismissing hopes that Pyongyang could eventually surrender its nuclear weapons. Kim Yo Jong made the remarks on Thursday, insisting that North Korea’s nuclear status was permanent and could not be reversed through diplomatic pressure. North Korea has legally established itself as a nuclear weapons state, with its leadership maintaining that its nuclear arsenal is permanent and irreversible. Advertisement US President Donald Trump said in August that North Korea possessed 57 “very powerful” nuclear weapons, while South Korea has estimated the country’s arsenal at between 80 and 120 warheads. Kim Yo Jong’s comments came as South Korea said it was closely monitoring developments, particularly because Trump has recently raised the possibility of another meeting with Kim Jong Un. “The DPRK’s position as a nuclear weapons state is absolute which can not reverse with anything,” Kim Yo Jong said in a statement carried by the official Korean Central News Agency. Advertisement She argued that North Korea’s nuclear arsenal plays an important role in deterring what she described as hostile actions by other countries. Pyongyang’s nuclear weapons, she said, “makes a significant contribution to deterring the outrageous acts of international rogues.” Her remarks came during the General Conference of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) in Vienna, where she also dismissed renewed discussions about denuclearising North Korea. Advertisement Kim Yo Jong said the “familiar silly talk” about efforts to denuclearise the country was expected. “If they believe that it is really possible, they will only hear the word of idiots,” she said. She further insisted that neither political statements nor international opposition could alter North Korea’s nuclear status. Advertisement “No matter how rhetorically the hostile forces may deny, the reality in which the nuclear position of the DPRK has been permanently settled physically and legally cannot change even a bit,” she added, using the acronym for the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea, North Korea’s official name. A South Korean Unification Ministry official said Kim Yo Jong’s statement was significant because of its timing, coming amid renewed discussion about US-North Korea diplomacy. “We are paying close attention to Kim Yo Jong’s statement, as it comes at a time when US President Donald Trump has recently expressed his willingness to pursue dialogue with North Korea,” the official said, according to a transcript obtained by AFP. Advertisement Trump has repeatedly said he is open to restarting talks with Kim Jong Un and said last month that he planned to meet the North Korean leader later this year. Trump and Kim met three times during Trump’s first term, but their diplomatic engagement stalled following the 2019 summit in Hanoi. The Hanoi meeting ended without an agreement on sanctions relief or what North Korea would provide in return for denuclearisation. Advertisement Since the collapse of those talks, Pyongyang has continued expanding its nuclear arsenal. Opinion Nigeria News Advertisement

entries.title: KIEV – Zelensky synon marrëveshje për dronë dhe lidhje më të ngushta me Japoninë në teknologjinë e mbrojtjes – 24 ore
entries.paragraph_1: KIEV, 17 shtator /ATSH -AA/ – Presidenti ukrainas, Volodymyr Zelenskyy ka bërë të ditur se Ukraina dëshiron të zgjerojë bashkëpunimin me Japoninë në fushën e teknologjisë së mbrojtjes, përfshirë përmes një marrëveshjeje të propozuar për dronë.
entries.paragraph_2: Në një intervistë për transmetuesin japonez NHK, Zelenskyy tha se kompanitë japoneze mund të përfitojnë nga përvoja e Ukrainës në mbikëqyrjen detare, zbulimin, çminimin, mbrojtjen ajrore dhe sigurinë kibernetike. “Ne dëshirojmë shumë të ndërtojmë bashkëpunim ushtarako-teknologjik midis Ukrainës dhe Japonisë”, tha ai duke shprehur interes për partneritete si në nivel qeveritar, ashtu edhe në atë të biznesit.

entries.title: Бракът Путин-Ким Чен-ун обърка сметките на Си Цзинпин - Свят — Новини Стандарт
entries.paragraph_1: Един от най-неочакваните геополитически ефекти на войната в Украйна започва да се усеща не в Европа, а на другия край на Евразия. Задълбочаващото се военно партньорство между Владимир Путин и Ким Чен-ун дава на Северна Корея пари, технологии и политическа свобода, каквито режимът в Пхенян не е имал от години, а това все повече тревожи Китай. entries.paragraph_2: Русия плаща огромна цена за продължителната война в Украйна. Разходите на Москва се оценяват на приблизително 290 млрд. долара годишно и тя има загуби от около 30 000 военнослужещи месечно. Руското настъпление е спряло или се забавя по отделни направления, а икономическата тежест на конфликта все по-силно достига до населението.

entries.title: Beef Export Value Strong while Pork Exports below Year-Ago - Southeast AgNET
entries.paragraph_1: U.S. beef exports delivered another strong month in July, according to data released by the USDA and compiled by the U.S. Meat Export Federation . Export volume held steady at just over 89,000 metric tons, while export value climbed 6% from a year ago to nearly $797 million. Strong demand from Taiwan, Mexico, Japan, the Middle East, Colombia, the Caribbean, and Southeast Asia helped drive those gains.
entries.paragraph_2: USMEF President and CEO Dan Halstrom says global demand for U.S. beef remains resilient despite ongoing challenges in China. While exports in China remain well below previous years’ levels, growth in other international markets continue to support overall beef demand. For the first seven months of the year, beef exports totaled nearly 635,000 metric tons, valued at $5.5 billion.
